#354 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · reports · Ibn Kathir says Ibn Jarir also transmits the earlier report through Asbat. «ورواه ابن جرير، من حديث أسباط، به. (7)»
#355 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · holds · Ibn Kathir calls the report strange because this verse is Meccan whereas al-Aqra and Uyayna converted long after the Hijra. «وهذا حديث غريب، فإن هذه الآية مكية، والأقرع بن حابس وعيينة إنما أسلما بعد الهجرة بدهر»
#356 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · سعد · reports · Sa’d says the verse concerned six Companions, including Ibn Masud, who arrived early and drew near to hear the Prophet; Quraysh objected to their proximity. «نزلت هذه الآية في ستة من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، منهم ابن مسعود»
#357 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · Those the Prophet must not drive away are poor Muslims, devoted to their Lord in contrast to unbelievers who call on powerless beings. «عكس ما عليه الكفار في دعاء من لا يملك لهم ضرا ولا نفعا»
#358 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · Morning and evening may mean both ends of each day, the two daily prayers, or continuous worship; their long constancy indicates sincerity rather than ostentation. «في طرفي النهار مطلقا أو بصلاتيهما أو يكون كناية عن الدوام»
#359 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · The wealthy polytheists promised to follow Muhammad if he expelled his humble companions, whom they disparaged as insincere and driven by need. «وعدوه صلى الله عليه وسلم الاتباع إن طرد من تبعه ممن يأنفون من مجالستهم»
#360 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · The Prophet has no stake in worldly gain from expelling the poor or accepting the rich; his mission calls people away from worldly life. «التي هو مبعوث للتنفير عنها»
#361 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · The denial of responsibility for one another's account means the Prophet sees only outward conduct; he need not expel them over a fear that they are insincere or that they burden him. «ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء»
#362 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · An alternative reading of the denial of mutual accounting, linked to 18:28, concerns provision: the Prophet's invitation is for the afterlife, and neither the poor nor the Prophet depends on the other's provision. «يعني أن دعاءك إلى الله إنما مداره الأمر الأخروي»
#363 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · reports · The author adduces lexicons and usage showing that hisab can mean sufficiency or provision: 78:36 gives an abundant gift; the verb can mean feeding to satisfaction; and a report from Simak says hosts did not honor their guest. «صاحب القاموس وغيره : الحساب : الكافي»
#364 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · أبو عبيد الهروي · reports · Abu Ubayd explains ahsabtuhu as giving someone enough until he says, “That suffices me.” «أي أعطيته الكفاية حتى قال»
#365 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · reports · The phrase “without account” in 2:212 means without stinting or constriction; Ibn Faris likewise glosses ahsabtuhu as giving enough or what satisfies. «بغير تقتير وتضييق , وفي حديث سماك»
#366 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · Expelling the poor would be unjustly putting things out of place and would not make the wealthy polytheists believe; guidance belongs to God alone. «وليس هدايتهم إلا إلينا»
#367 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · God tested groups through the Prophet's appointment and through differences of faith, wealth, and poverty; elites scorned the poor as unworthy of God's favor. «بالتخصيص بالإيمان والغنى والفقر ونحو ذلك» [filed under 6:52-53]
#368 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · The elite's objection anticipates their later demand to receive what God's messengers received; God alone knows who merits preference through gratitude. «فالآية ناظرة إلى ما يأتي في هذه السورة من قوله تعالى» [filed under 6:52-53]
#369 DURR-FULL d.911 · عبد الله بن مسعود · reports · Quraysh leaders asked the Prophet to expel poor Muslim companions such as Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, and Khabbab so that they might follow him; the warning verse was revealed. «عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال مر الملأ من قريش على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعنده صهيب وعمار وبلال وخباب»
#370 DURR-FULL d.911 · عكرمة · reports · Quraysh nobles asked Abu Talib to have Muhammad expel poor and enslaved followers so they would join; Umar suggested testing their request, then verses about not expelling the believers were revealed. «عن عكرمة قال مشى عتبة بن ربيعة وشيبة بن ربيعة وقرظة بن عبد عمر وبن نوفل» [filed under 6:52, 6:53]
#371 SUYUTI-LUBAB d.911 · خباب · reports · Khabbab reports that Aqra ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn asked the Prophet to dismiss poor believers such as Suhayb, Bilal, Ammar, and Khabbab when Arab delegations arrived; the verse forbidding their expulsion was revealed. «جاء الأقرع ابن حابس وعيينة بن حصن فوجدا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع صهيب وبلال وعمار وخباب قاعدا في ناس من الضعفاء»
#372 SUYUTI-LUBAB d.911 · ابن كثير · rejects · Ibn Kathir calls the report unusual because the verse is Meccan while Aqra and Uyayna converted much later, after the Hijra. «قال ابن كثير هذا حديث غريب فإن الآية مكية والأقرع وعيينة إنما أسلما بعد الهجرة بدهر»
#373 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · ‘Seeking His face’ is circumstantial to ‘they call’; it stresses that sincerity is the essential point of supplication. «يدعونه تعالى مخلصين له وقيد الدعاء بالإخلاص تنبيها على أنه ملاك الأمر»
#374 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · A Persian couplet says worship is good when intention is sincere; without that, it is like a kernel-less grain. «عبادت بإخلاص نيت نكوست وكرنه ه آيد زبى مغزوست»
#375 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · Seeking God's face is among the strongest grounds for honor and is incompatible with expelling poor worshippers. «من أقوى موجبات الإكرام المنافي للأبعاد»
#376 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · Quraysh not only disparaged poor believers' status but alleged their faith was false and that they gathered for food and clothing; God rejects this as grounds for expulsion. «في طعن فقراء المسلمين على وصفهم بكونهم موالي ومساكين بل طعنوا في إيمانهم»
#377 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · The Prophet must judge by their outward mark of piety; any hidden defect in faith harms only them, not him, so he should welcome and nurture them. «ليس عليك إلا اعتبار ظاهر حالهم وهو اتسامهم بسمة المتقين»
#378 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · The repeated denial of responsibility emphasizes that their reckoning is no concern of the Prophet, just as his is no concern of theirs. «مع أن الجواب قد تم بما قبله للمبالغة في بيان انتفاء كون حسابهم عليه»
#379 BURSEVI d.1127 · أبو السعود · reports · Abū al-Suʿūd says the repeated phrase emphasizes the point by pairing it with the uncontroversial reverse; ‘then you expel them’ answers the prohibition's logic. «قال المولى أبو السعود : وذكر قوله تعالى»
#380 BURSEVI d.1127 · السري السقطي · reports · Al-Sarī al-Saqaṭī says he found Bahlūl in a cemetery; Bahlūl replied that the dead do not harm him or gossip when he is away. «خرجت يوما إلى المقابر فإذا ببهلول فقلت له أي شيء تصنع هنا»
#381 BURSEVI d.1127 · بهلول · reports · Bahlūl left when hungry and recited that hunger is a pious act and prolonged hunger will eventually be followed by satisfaction. «أجالس قوما لا يؤذونني وإن غبت لا يغتابونني»
#382 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · A king's parable shows God adorning chosen lovers with righteous deeds and pure states: they need not display themselves to ordinary people, since God knows and their rank will be seen at the great gathering. «فهذا مثل من وفقهم الله تعالى للأعمال الصالحة والأحوال الزكية ولا حاجة لهم»
#383 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · A Persian couplet contrasts the noble servants of God with the speaker's group as wretched slaves. «أولئك خدام كرام وسادة ونحن عبيد السوء بئس عبيد»
#384 BURSEVI d.1127 · reports · Quraysh leaders asked the Prophet to expel poor wool-clad believers such as Ṣuhayb, ʿAmmār, Khabbāb, Bilāl, and Salmān so they could retain his company and status before Arab visitors. «حين رأوا في مجلسه الشريف فقراء المؤمنين»
#385 BURSEVI d.1127 · رسول الله · reports · The Prophet refused to expel believers, though he considered separating them to attract Quraysh; revelation taught that religion does not privilege the rich over the poor. «ما أنا بطارد المؤمنين»
#386 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · Expulsion means removal; morning and evening remembrance signifies continuity, and whoever remembers continually remains with God. «الطرد الإبعاد وبالفارسية»
#387 BURSEVI d.1127 · النبي · reports · The Prophet says, ‘I am the companion of whoever remembers Me.’ «أنا جليس من ذكرني»
#388 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · The poor worshippers seek God's face and pleasure alone, not worldly aims. «بذكرهم وعبادتهم {وجهه} تعالى ورضاه لا شيئا من أغراض الدنيا»
#389 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · ‘Thus We tested them’ points to God's giving poor believers precedence in religion by granting faith despite their poor worldly condition, while the rich had worldly precedence. «ذلك إشارة إلى مصدر ما بعده من الفعل»
#390 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · The prefixed kāf intensifies the demonstrative: God tried them with a complete and remarkable trial. «والكاف مقحمة لتأكيد ما أفاده اسم الإشارة من الفخامة»
#391 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · holds · After commanding the Prophet to warn the people who may become pious, God forbids doing so in a way that would lead him to expel the poor believers. «لما أمر النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بانذار المذكورين لعلهم ينتظمون في سلك المتقين نهى»
#392 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · reports · Some accounts suggest the warning and no-expulsion verses came down together, while others do not indicate that. «ويفهم من بعض الروايات أن الآيتين نزلتا معا»
#393 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · ابن مسعود · reports · Ibn Masud reports Quraysh leaders seeing Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, Khabbab, and other poor Muslims with the Prophet and demanding their expulsion, promising they might then follow him; the Quran was revealed concerning this. «مر الملأ من قريش على»
#394 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · خباب · reports · Khabbab reports that al-Aqraʿ and ʿUyayna looked down on the poor believers and demanded private access for tribal leaders, promising to meet the Prophet with the poor later; after Gabriel delivered the verse, the Prophet called the believers to him and then stayed with them when rising. «جاء الأقرع بن حابس التميمي وعيينة بن حصن الفزاري»

#395 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · عكرمة · reports · Ikrima reports that Quraysh nobles asked Abu Talib to have Muhammad expel poor slaves and allies so they would follow him; Umar suggested doing so temporarily, and verses warning and identifying the grateful were revealed, after which Umar apologized. «مشى عتبة وشيبة أبنا ربيعة وقرظة بن عبد عمرو»
#396 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · عكرمة · reports · The report names the poor believers as Bilal, ʿAmmar, Salim, Subayh, Ibn Masʿud, al-Miqdad, Waqid, ʿAmr, and Marthad, with allies and freedmen among them. «وكانوا بلالا وعمار بن ياسر وسالم مولى»
#397 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · عكرمة · reports · The report says the verse 'Thus We have tried some of them by others' addressed Quraysh leaders and their clients; when it came, Umar apologized, and 'When those who believe in Our signs come to you' was revealed. «وكذلك فتنا بعضهم ببعض»
#398 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · holds · Al-ghadah derives from ghudwah with the waw changing to alif; al-ashi derives from ashwa with waw changing to ya and assimilation. The author says al-ashi appears singular like ashiyyah, though some call it a plural. «وأصل العشي عشوى قلبت الواو ياء»
#399 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · holds · Some say al-ashi is a plural of ashiyyah, but the author finds this far-fetched; morning means early morning or the time from dawn prayer until sunrise, and evening means the end of the day. «هو جمع عشية وفيه بعد ومعنى الأول لغة البكرة»
#400 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · reports · Morning and evening can denote continual practice, or the acts of supplication, prayer, remembrance, or Qur'an recitation; the temporal terms can stand for what occurs at those times, and prayer can also mean its time or place. «والمراد بالدعاء حقيقته أو الصلاة أو الذكر أو قراءة القرآن أقوال»
#401 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · مجاهد · reports · Mujahid interprets morning and evening as the dawn and afternoon prayers; the times are named for the prayers, which are singled out for their honor. «عن مجاهد أنهما عبارة عن صلاتي الصبح والعصر»
#402 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · ابن عامر · reports · Ibn ʿAmir, also in al-Kahf, and several other readers recite الغدوة with a wāw; Abu ʿUbayd calls that reading an error because he treats ghudwah as a proper name that cannot take the article. «ابن عامر هنا وفي الكهف»
#403 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · rejects · The author rejects Abu Ubayd criticism: ghudwah is also attested as a common noun with the article, as reported from al-Khalil by Sibawayh, al-Mubarrad, and other language authorities; the transmitted reading itself suffices as evidence. «منكرا مصروفا فتدخلها أل حينئذ»
#404 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · holds · The verse does not establish that the Prophet actually expelled anyone; reports say he considered assigning separate times to the devoted poor and Quraysh leaders to draw the latter toward faith, without humiliating the believers. «والذي تحكيه اة ثار أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام هم أن يجعل لاولئك الداعين المتقين وقتا خاصا»
#405 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · المشهور · reports · The common interpretation takes God's face as His essence, hence the believers seek Him sincerely; the author notes that this interpretation must explain how God can be willed if will attaches only to possible things. «فقيل وهو المشهور إنه الذات أي مريدين ذاته تعالى»
#406 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · الزجاج · reports · Al-Zajjaj interprets God's face as the direction or path He commands them to seek. «المراد به الجهة والطريق والمعنى مريدين الطريق»
#407 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · الإمام · reports · Another interpretation takes seeking God's face as a metaphor for love and seeking His approval; the author says this account is questionable. «إنه كناية عن المحبة وطلب الرضا»

#431 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · الواحدي · reports · Al-Wahidi identifies the four unnamed companions in Sa'd's account as Suhayb, Ammar ibn Yasir, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and Khabbab ibn al-Aratt. «وسمى الواحدي بقية الستة : وهم صهيب ، وعمار بن ياسر»
#432 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · البيهقي · reports · Al-Bayhaqi's fuller account says Quraysh chiefs proposed removing poor believers while they visited and restoring them afterward; the Prophet refused, then agreed to the arrangement hoping they would believe, and the verse came. «ما رواه البيهقي أن رؤساء قريش قالوا لرسول الله : لو طردت هؤلاء»
#433 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · ابن ماجة · reports · A report in Ibn Majah, from Khabbab, names al-Aqra ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn as the men who made the expulsion request and cause of revelation. «ووقع في ( سنن ) ابن ماجة عن خباب أن قائل ذلك للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم»
#434 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · ابن عطية · reports · Ibn Atiyya calls the Ibn Majah attribution unlikely because this is a Meccan verse and the two men came with the Banu Tamim delegation in Medina. «وقال ابن عطية : هو بعيد لأن الآية مكية . وعيينة والأقرع إنما وفدا»
#435 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The two men may have made a similar request later, and the Prophet answered it with the verse originally revealed about an analogous proposal. «ولعل ذلك وقع منهما فأجابهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بهذه الآية»
#436 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · Their invocation publicly professed faith in God alone, implying conviction; hypocrisy had not appeared before the community in Medina. «ومعنى { يدعون ربهم } يعلنون إيمانهم به دون الأصنام إعلانا بالقول ، وهو يستلزم اعتقاد القائل بما يقوله ، إذ لم يكن يومئذ نفاق وإنما ظهر المنافقون بالمدينة .»
#437 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · Al-ghadāh is early morning and al-ʿashiyy spans noon to dawn; the generic terms and temporal bāʾ mean they invoke God throughout the day and all days. «والمعنى أنهم يدعون الله اليوم كله . فالغداة والعشي قصد بهما استيعاب الزمان والأيام كما يقصد بالمشرق والمغرب استيعاب الأمكنة»
#438 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · قيل · reports · An alternative takes invocation as prayer and morning and evening as all times of the five daily prayers, so the prohibition means not to expel worshippers, that is, believers. «وقيل : أريد بالدعاء الصلاة . وبالغداة والعشي عموم أوقات الصلوات الخمس . فالمعنى ولا تطرد المصلين ، أي المؤمنين .»
#439 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · reports · Most readers pronounce al-ghadāh with an open ghayn and long ā; Ibn ʿĀmir reads a rounded ghayn, silent dāl, and long wāw, a dialect form. «وقرأ الجمهور { بالغداة } بفتح الغين وبألف بعد الدال . وقرأه ابن عامر بضم الغين وسكون الدال وبواو ساكنة بعد الدال وهي لغة في الغداة .»
#440 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The clause about seeking His face is circumstantial and means they invoke God sincerely for His pleasure, seeking no worldly advantage. «وجملة { يريدون وجهه } حال من الضمير المرفوع في { يدعون } ، أي يدعون مخلصين يريدون وجه الله ، أي لا يريدون حظا دنيويا .»
#441 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · Face literally names the part of the head with the sensory organs and can stand metonymically for the whole essence. «والوجه حقيقة الجزء من الرأس الذي فيه العينان والأنف والفم . ويطلق الوجه على الذات كلها مجازا مرسلا .»
#442 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · Here face is a metaphor for the essence, with an implicit modifier; the meaning is seeking God’s pleasure rather than pleasing anyone else. «والوجه هنا مستعار للذات على اعتبار مضاف ، أي يريدون رضى الله ، أي لا يريدون إرضاء غيره .»
#443 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · rejects · Although it was said that Quraysh accused poor believers of hypocrisy, no sound report supports this; the phrase most likely praises their complete faith rather than answering that accusation. «وقد قيل : إن قريشا طعنوا في إيمان الضعفاء ونسبوهم إلى النفاق ، إلا أن هذا لم يرد به أثر صحيح ، فالأظهر»
#444 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The following clause may explain why the believers must not be expelled or invalidate the rationale for seeking their expulsion; since invalidating the forbidden act’s rationale becomes a reason for the prohibition, the sentence is separated. «وجملة { ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء } تعليل للنهي عن طردهم ، أو إبطال لعلة الهم بطردهم ، أو لعلة طلب طردهم . فإن إبطال علة فعل المنهي عنه يؤول إلى كونه تعليلا للنهي ، ولذا فصلت هذه الجملة .»
#445 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The Prophet is not responsible for whether polytheists believe; their account belongs elsewhere, so he must not deprive believers of their rights to secure others' conversion. «ما عليك من حساب المشركين على الإيمان بك أو على عدم الإيمان شيء»
#446 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The genitive in 'their accounting' can mean either the Prophet's reckoning of them or the polytheists' reckoning of believers' poverty and weakness. «وعلى هذا الوجه يجوز كون إضافة { حسابهم } من إضافة المصدر إلى مفعوله»
#447 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The fronted predicate with عَلَى conveys obligation or burden and corrects a possible inclination to yield to Quraysh's chiefs. «و ( على ) فيه دالة على معنى اللزوم والوجوب لأن الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام»
#448 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The preposition من is redundant for emphasis, specifying the comprehensive scope of the negation under لا. «و ( من ) في قوله : { من شيء } زائدة لتوكيد النفي للتنصيص على الشمول»
#449 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · Fronting the predicates is optional because the following indefinite subjects occur under negation; it may convey emphasis or restriction, and al-Kashshaf favors restriction. «فلا بد له من غرض . والغرض يحتمل مجرد الاهتمام ويحتمل الاختصاص»
#450 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · On the restrictive reading, only God accounts for the believers; the negated account is confined to the Prophet, as in the restrictive reading of 37:47. «قصر نفي حسابهم على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليفيد أن حسابهم على غيره»
#451 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · A poetic example uses أحرزوا for the polytheists' seizure of the Muslims' collected spoils. «أي أحرز المشركون ما جمعه المسلمون من الغنائم»
#452 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The verse accumulates five emphases: two uses of من, fronting, restrictive wording, and completion by negating the reciprocal account, to utterly disavow yielding to the request. «وقد اجتمع في هذا الكلام خمسة مؤكدات . وهي ( من ) البيانية ، و ( من ) الزائدة»
#453 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The address indirectly exposes Quraysh chiefs' claim that poor believers kept them from the Prophet; if sincere, they should attend without judging others, as clarified in 6:55. «ويفيد هذا الكلام التعريض برؤساء قريش الذين سألوا إبعاد الفقراء عن مجلس الرسول»
#454 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The implied affirmative counterpart is that each person is accountable for himself; no believer should lose a right to satisfy the Prophet or someone seeking faith. «كل نفس بما كسبت رهينة»
#455 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The warning resembles the conditional address in which even the Prophet's work would be void if he associated partners with God. «فيكون الخطاب على نحو قوله تعالى : { لئن أشركت ليحبطن عملك } ( الزمر : 65 )»
#456 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The repeated verb is a subjunctive result of the prohibition; repeating expulsion reinforces the command and reconnects it to the later warning after intervening material. «لإفادة تأكيد ذلك النهي وليبنى عليه قوله { فتكون من الظالمين } لوقوع»
#457 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The verb may instead answer the preceding negation: do not expel them merely to satisfy their enemies' wish. «على أنه يجوز أن يجعل { فتطردهم } منصوبا في جواب النفي من قوله : { ما عليك من حسابهم»
#458 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · Being among wrongdoers follows from expelling believers to please others; the threat also characterizes the requesters as proud people disposed to injustice. «وإنما جعل طردهم ظلما لأنه لما انتفى تكليفه بأن يحاسبهم»
#459 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · A second parsing makes 'you would be among wrongdoers' the result of the prohibition, with the repeated expulsion clause serving as a resumptive link after a long interruption. «ويجوز أن يجعل قوله : { فتكون من الظالمين } منصوبا في جواب النهي»
#460 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The reciprocal clause indirectly accuses the polytheists of disguising pride as advice, pretending expulsion would win them over while claiming concern for the Prophet. «وفي قوله : { وما من حسابك عليهم من شيء } تعريض بالمشركين بأنهم أظهروا»
#461 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · rejects · The meaning is not that both groups' accounts belong to God: that reading is out of context and makes the second clause redundant, unlike Noah's reported statement. «ثم بهذا يظهر أن ليس المعنى : بل حسابهم على الله وحسابك على الله ، لأن هذا غير مناسب»
#462 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · Alternatively, fronting may simply emphasize that the Prophet bears no obligation, since restriction does not clearly fit the believers who invoke God. «مجرد الاهتمام بنفي اللزوم والوجوب الذي دل عليه حرف ( على )»
#463 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The reciprocal clause is added to complete the rationale; the first clause receives priority because its application to the Prophet and the requesters is the main point. «وإنما جيء بالجملة الثانية لاستكمال التعليل كما تقدم»

#468 TABATABAI d.1402 · عمر بن عبد الله بن المهاجر · reports · A report says the verse came after some people proposed that the Prophet expel the poor Companions of the Suffa. «عن عمر بن عبد الله بن المهاجر أن الآية نزلت في اقتراح بعض الناس»

#471 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · God has no bodily face or material direction; “face” is what something faces others with, so it can metaphorically denote the direction or aspect by which it is encountered. «لكن وجه الشيء لما كان ما يستقبل به غيره كانت الجهة بمعنى الناحية»
#472 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · Righteous works can be a face oriented toward God, while evil works face Satan; divine attributes and names are also ways creation encounters God. «وبهذه العناية تصير الأعمال الصالحة وجها لله تعالى كما أن الأعمال الطالحة وجه للشيطان»

#474 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · Anything related to divine nearness—God's names, attributes, religion, good deeds, prophets, angels, martyrs, and forgiven believers—is a face of God. «وكذا كل من يحل في ساحة قربه كالأنبياء والملائكة والشهداء وكل مغفور له من المؤمنين وجه له تعالى»

#478 TABATABAI d.1402 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم · reports · A report calls those who deny divine decree and claim independent human will and power the Magians of this community. «قال فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم " ألا إن لكل أمه مجوسا»

#482 TABATABAI d.1402 · عبد الله بن مسعود · reports · Ibn Mas'ud reports that Quraysh leaders asked the Prophet to expel poor Muslims such as Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, and Khabbab so they might follow him. «مر الملأ من قريش على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وعنده صهيب وعمار وبلال وخباب» [filed under 6:51, 6:52]
#483 TABATABAI d.1402 · بعض المفسرين · reports · Some commentators say the people singled out are believers who affirm resurrection and are the poor believers mentioned in the next verse. «في المؤمنين القائلين بالحشر، وأنهم هم الذين عنوا في الآية التالية» [filed under 6:51, 6:52]
#484 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · The context indicates that Meccan polytheists asked the Prophet to expel poor believers; this resembles elites in Noah's community demanding the same of him. «أن المشركين من قومه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم اقترحوا عليه أن يطرد عن نفسه الضعفاء المؤمنين به» [filed under 6:52, 6:53]
#485 ASAD-NOTES d.1412 · reports · Traditions place the revelation of this and the next verse after Meccan pagan leaders offered to consider Islam if Muhammad dismissed former slaves and other low-status followers; he rejected their demand. «some of the pagan chieftains at Mecca expressed their willingness to consider accepting Islam on the condition»
#486 ASAD-NOTES d.1412 · holds · Asad says the historical occasion is not a full explanation: the verse's wording concerns people who believe in God and seek His grace, even if they are not Muslims in the current sense. «while not being Muslims in the current sense of this word»
#487 ASAD-NOTES d.1412 · holds · The enduring instruction applies to all Qur'an followers: do not repel anyone who believes in God, even with incomplete Qur'anic beliefs; instead explain the teaching patiently. «they are enjoined not to repulse anyone who believes in God - even though his beliefs may not fully answer»
#488 ASAD-NOTES d.1412 · holds · The reciprocal accountability clause means people answer to God alone for beliefs or conduct that differ from Qur'anic teaching. «all are accountable to God alone»
#489 ASAD-NOTES d.1412 · holds · The literal phrase means that repelling them would make the addressee one of the evildoers. «so that thou shouldst repulse them and thus be of the evildoers»
#490 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · In the four-sūrah sequence, al-An‘ām conclusively presents truth to Quraysh, while al-A‘rāf warns them. «Sūrah al-An‘ām conclusively communicates the truth to the Quraysh. Sūrah al-A‘rāf sounds a warning to them.» [filed under 6:1-165]
#491 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Al-Anfāl prepares believers for jihād and announces Quraysh's removal from custodianship of the House of God. «the divine decision is taken to depose the Quraysh from the custodianship of the House of God.» [filed under 6:1-165]
#492 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Al-Tawbah issues Quraysh an ultimatum and gives the Hypocrites a final warning. «an ultimatum is sounded to the Quraysh and the Hypocrites are given a final warning.» [filed under 6:1-165]
#493 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Qur’an Group 1 primarily addresses the People of the Book and only secondarily Quraysh; Group 2 reverses that order. «Group 1 of the Qur’ ān is directed to the People of the Book. If the Quraysh are addressed, it is only in a secondary way.» [filed under 6:1-165]
#494 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Group 2 argues mainly from human nature, intellect, and the world, whereas Group 1 uses matters the People of the Book acknowledged. «In Group 2, arguments are mostly drawn from the signs found in human nature and intellect and in the world around human beings.» [filed under 6:1-165]
#495 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · In Group 1 believers replace the People of the Book as religious leaders; in Group 2 they replace Quraysh as custodians of the House. «In Group 1, the People of the Book are deposed from religious leadership and their place has been given to the believers.» [filed under 6:1-165]
#496 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The sūrah invites Quraysh to monotheism, the hereafter, and Muhammad’s prophethood, warning them with the fate of nations that rejected messengers and using Abraham’s argument to identify his true followers. «They are invited to profess faith while arguments in favour of monotheism, the hereafter» [filed under 6:1-165]
#497 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · This section tells Muhammad to leave sign-demanders, warn those fearing God and the hereafter, and preserve access for poor believers rather than appease arrogant elites. «those who were demanding signs and punishments. However, he should warn through this book those who fear God and the hereafter.» [filed under 6:51-55]
#498 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The believers seeking religious understanding are worthy of the Prophet’s attention, while the poor’s presence is itself a trial for wealthy opponents. «Nor should he turn away the poor among the believers merely to please these arrogant elements.» [filed under 6:51-55]
#499 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The Prophet is not accountable for arrogant people’s refusal, and neither are they accountable for his duties in a way that could justify his turning believers away; doing so would be injustice. «Similarly, these people will not be held responsible on the Day of Judgement for the duties imposed on him»
#500 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Muhammad must not abandon sincere worshippers to appease wealthy, arrogant people who disparage his poor companions. «he should not waste any more time on the wretched among them who are inebriated by their status»
<<part 12 ends; continues in part 13>>

#501 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Quraysh leaders disparaged the companions as poor menial workers and argued that respectable people could not join a religion that welcomed them; Muhammad must not lose true companions to win these elites. «his companions were all poor who did menial jobs and how could God select such lowly sections of the society for His religion»
#502 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · If the elites persist in error, they alone bear its consequence; turning away genuine seekers would leave the Prophet liable for neglecting those deserving his care. «If he goes after these wretched elements, they will not be held responsible on his behalf»
#503 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Addressing Muhammad rather than the Quraysh directly strikes at their arrogance and implies they are unworthy of direct address. «instead of addressing them, the Prophet (sws) is addressed. This is to make evident to them that they are not even worthy of being addressed directly.»
#504 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The verb used for driving the poor away is harsh and means to disregard someone disparagingly, matching what Quraysh wanted Muhammad to do to his companions. «it means to disparagingly disregard someone.»
#505 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · Jesus (sws) · reports · Jesus’ lost-sheep parable depicts a shepherd seeking one straying sheep instead of being content with the ninety-nine. «Jesus (sws) has stated a parable also: “What do you think? If a man owns a hundred sheep»
#506 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The lost-sheep parable illustrates God’s affection for people who return after error and a prophet’s concern for his nation’s faith. «Just as this parable shows the great affection God has for people who turn to Him after being in error»
#507 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The Prophet should warn those who fear God and the hereafter, ignore demands for miracles, and welcome poor believers seeking God’s pleasure without turning them away to attract arrogant elites. «As for those who seek God’s pleasure and want to listen to his message, he must not distance them from himself» [filed under 6:51-55]
#508 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · Prophetic concern for people reflects God’s affection and is praiseworthy, but it has limits: the Prophet must not pursue the wayward at the expense of loyal companions. «God does not want his prophet to go after those people who have gone astray at the expense of his real companions.»
#509 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · reports · Farāhī discusses important points on this topic in his commentary on Sūrah ‘Abas; Islahi says he will give his own view later. «Ustādh Far āhī has written some very important points related to this topic in his exegesis of Sūrah ‘Abas.»
#510 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The poor believers seek only their Creator’s pleasure, so the promised mercy and forgiveness answer their actual desire rather than worldly status or riches. «The only desire they had was to please their creator and master.» [filed under 6:52, 6:54]
#511 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · reports · A report in Muslim and other hadith collections says Quraysh notables demanded the poor, vulnerable Companions leave before they would meet Muhammad; he refused, then considered their lesser demand before this verse stopped him. «Müslim’in Sahîh’i (“Fezâilü’s-sahâbe”, 45-46) ve diğer bazı hadis kaynaklarında yer alan bir rivayete göre»
#512 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · Habbâb · reports · After the verse, the Prophet and poor Muslims grew so close that they sat knee to knee, and he waited for them to rise before leaving so as not to hurt them. «Habbâb’ın anlattığına göre bu âyetin inmesinden sonra Hz. Peygamber’le yoksul ve kimsesiz müslümanlar arasındaki yakınlık o kadar artmıştır»
#513 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · müfessirlerin çoğu · rejects · Most commentators, noting reports that the whole surah descended at once rather than in parts, deny that this verse was occasioned by that incident; even if so, the incident only occasions its universal ethical teaching. «müfessirlerin çoğu bu sûrenin, parça parça değil, tamamının bir defada indiğini bildiren haberleri de dikkate alarak»
#514 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · some interpreters · reports · Some interpreters take the pronoun ‘they’ in the accountability clause to refer to the polytheists. «“Onların hesaplarından sana sorumluluk yoktur...” cümlesindeki “onlar” zamiriyle müşriklere işaret edildiğini düşünenler olmuşsa da»
#515 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · ağırlıklı görüş · prefers · The predominant view is that ‘they’ refers to the poor Muslims mentioned earlier. «ağırlıklı görüş, bununla yukarıda anılan müslümanların kastedildiği yönündedir»
#516 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · müşrikler · reports · The polytheists alleged that the poor Muslims gathered around the Prophet for shelter, food, and drink rather than sincere devotion. «Rivayete göre müşrikler, Hz. Peygamber’in çevresinde toplanan söz konusu kişilerin, aslında –samimi dindarlıklarından değil– barınma imkânı buldukları, yiyip içtikleri için orada toplandıklarını ileri sürmüşlerdi»
#517 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · one view · reports · One interpretation says the verse separates the Prophet’s responsibility from the poor Muslims’ responsibility: each bears their own deeds, so he should remain close to them rather than wrong them. «herkesin kendi yapıp ettiklerinin sorumluluğunu yine kendisinin taşıdığı bildirilerek Resûl-i Ekrem’in onlara olan ilgisini sürdürmesi istenmiş»
#518 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · another interpretation · reports · Another reading says the Prophet should not send worshipping poor people away to earn a living: their provision is God’s responsibility, not his calculation. «herkesin rızkını verenin Allah Teâlâ olduğuna işaret buyurulmuştur (Râzî, XII, 236-237)»
#519 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · holds · Human worth in Islam rests on faith, reverence for God, and spiritual nobility rather than rank, wealth, or lineage; the verse also shows the Prophet’s character formed by Qur’anic principles. «mevki, zenginlik ve soyuna göre değil iman zenginliğine, Allah’a saygı ve ruh yüceliğine göre değer taşıdığını ortaya koyması»
#520 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · holds · Humiliating people valued by God for faith and conduct is injustice, even if the hypothetical offender were a prophet. «farzımuhal bu kimse peygamber bile olsa– zalim olarak gösterilmesi son derece ilgi çekicidir»
#521 QIRAAT-ER · holds · Ghudwa as an instance noun contrasts with ghadāh as general morning, shifting from habitual to specific morning. «ghudwa (instance noun) vs ghadāh (general morning) — shifts from habitual to specific single-morning reading»
#522 STUDYQURAN · reports · Prominent Makkans wanted to join the Prophet’s teaching circle but disliked association with lower-status followers and asked him to send them away. «This verse was reportedly revealed when a group of prominent Makkans indicated that they wished to join the Prophet’s teaching circle»
#523 STUDYQURAN · al-Rāzī · reports · Al-Rāzī holds that the Prophet did not sin by initially appearing willing to accommodate the demand because his intention was good. «cannot be said to have sinned in his apparent initial willingness to accommodate the Makkans’ demand (R)»
#524 STUDYQURAN · R, Ṭ · reports · Morning and evening invocation may mean the five canonical prayers performed at their appointed times. «refer to praying the five canonical prayers at their prescribed times»
#525 STUDYQURAN · R, Ṭ · reports · Morning and evening invocation may mean supererogatory remembrance of God or Quran recitation. «performing supererogatory acts of invoking God»
#526 STUDYQURAN · R, Ṭ · reports · The invocation may include all these practices together. «or to all of them (R, Ṭ)»
#527 STUDYQURAN · R · reports · Desiring God’s Face can mean literally hoping to see it, as a sincere lover longs to see the beloved’s face. «with the hope of seeing God’s Face, for any sincere lover longs to see the face of the beloved (R)»
#528 STUDYQURAN · IK, R · reports · Desiring God’s Face can also metaphorically mean sincerity of intention among the Prophet’s followers. «it refers metaphorically to sincerity of intention among the Prophet’s followers (IK, R)»
#529 STUDYQURAN · holds · The verse echoes the Quranic principle that no person bears another’s burden. «echoes the Quranic idea that none shall bear the burden of another (6:164; 17:15; 35:18; 39:7; 53:38)»
#530 STUDYQURAN · Z · prefers · Syntactically, “their reckoning” most likely refers to the pious worshippers’ own reckoning, so the Prophet judges piety by outward acts. «that the Prophet need only judge his followers’ piety on the basis of their outward actions (Z)»
#531 STUDYQURAN · Some commentators · reports · Some commentators say the verse responds to a Quraysh accusation that the poor followed the Prophet for material support rather than religious sincerity. «Some commentators explain this as a response to an accusation made by some of the Quraysh»
#532 STUDYQURAN · R · reports · On that reading, the Prophet need not assess possible ulterior motives behind his followers’ apparent piety. «the verse was meant to indicate that the Prophet had no responsibility to assess the possible ulterior motives behind his»
#533 STUDYQURAN · Ṭ · reports · Some reports say the Makkans asked only that the poor followers be moved to the back rows of prayer, not expelled altogether. «Some reports indicate the Prophet was not asked to send away these followers altogether, but rather to send them to the back rows of prayer»
#534 STUDYQURAN · Z · prefers · More plausibly, the reckoning concerns the prominent Makkans; the Prophet need not court their conversion by yielding to their demand to dismiss sincere followers. «their embracing Islam that he should accede to their demand and “drive away”his pious followers at their behest (Z)»
<<part 13 ends; continues in part 14>>

<<notes for 6_52, part 14 of 0..14>>
#535 STUDYQURAN · holds · The Prophet refused to drive away his poorer followers, as Noah refused similar demands, though he was prepared to have them depart temporarily when prominent Makkans visited. «The Prophet refused to “drive away” his poorer followers (in 11:27–29 and 26:111–14 Noah refuses to do the same)»
#536 STUDYQURAN · IK, R, Ṭ, W · reports · The verse was revealed to forbid the Prophet from driving away his pious followers who worship morning and evening. «This verse was then revealed forbidding him from “driving away” his pious followers who call upon their Lord morning and evening (IK, R, Ṭ, W)»
#537 STUDYQURAN · Ṭ, W · reports · Quran 18:28 is linked to a similar circumstance and is reportedly a revelation about that situation. «reportedly revealed in a similar circumstance (Ṭ, W)»
#538 STUDYQURAN · holds · Quran 80:1–10 recounts the incident in which the Prophet is admonished for showing displeasure when a poor blind man came instead of wealthier Makkans. «about the incident in which the Prophet is admonished for registering displeasure when his teaching attracted a poor blind man rather than the wealthier Makkans»
#539 STUDYQURAN · holds · These passages raise the question of how the Prophet could appear to favor status-conscious Makkans over sincere followers, given that driving them away would make him a wrongdoer. «These passages raise the question of how the Prophet could seem to favor these prominent Makkans»
#540 STUDYQURAN · al-Rāzī · reports · Al-Rāzī says the Prophet’s possible initial willingness to accommodate the Makkans was intended only to facilitate their acceptance of Islam. «al-Rāzī argues that even if the Prophet were initially prepared to accede to the Makkans’ demand»
#541 STUDYQURAN · al-Rāzī · reports · Al-Rāzī reasons that the poor followers could be instructed another time, so no spiritual harm would come to them. «his intention was only to facilitate their acceptance of Islam, and since the Prophet could continue to instruct his poorer followers at another time»
#542 STUDYQURAN · holds · Al-Anʿām is Makkan and addresses the Prophet and Muslims' struggle with Makkan idolatry; its central aim is to refute idolatry and invented ritual practices. «al-Anʿām clearly addresses the challenges faced by the Prophet and the Muslims engaged in a religious struggle with the idolatrous Makkans» [filed under 6:1-165]
#543 STUDYQURAN · holds · The surah refutes worship of idols, celestial bodies, and jinn, and challenges the Makkans' invented religious practices. «The primary concern of the sūrah is to refute through powerful arguments various kinds of idolatry in general—including the worship of idols, celestial bodies, and jinn» [filed under 6:1-165]
#544 STUDYQURAN · Many · reports · Many regard it as a late Makkan surah, reflecting the Prophet's final effort to persuade the Makkans before his 622 migration to Madinah. «Many consider this sūrah to be a late Makkan one and thus to reflect the culmination of the Prophet’s struggle and effort to persuade the Makkans» [filed under 6:1-165]
#545 STUDYQURAN · holds · The Prophet is addressed throughout and given arguments and challenges for disbelievers; the surah sums up the Quranic case against idolatry. «The Prophet is directly addressed throughout the sūrah and given specific arguments and challenges to pose to the disbelievers in Makkah» [filed under 6:1-165]
#546 STUDYQURAN · reports · A hadith reports that al-Anʿām descended all at once with seventy thousand angels praising and glorifying God. «According to a ḥadīth, “Sūrat al-Anʿām was sent down all at once, accompanied by seventy thousand angels, hymning glorifications and praises”» [filed under 6:1-165]
#547 STUDYQURAN · al-Zamakhsharī · reports · A longer version adds that the seventy thousand angels seek forgiveness for whoever recites al-Anʿām with each verse, day and night. «A longer version of thisḥadīth cited by al-Zamakhsharī adds» [filed under 6:1-165]
